The following compilation represents a mere fraction of the vast and diverse world of fashion brands. While these selections offer a glimpse into various styles and designers, they are by no means exhaustive. Fashion is an ever-evolving landscape, rich with countless labels, each contributing uniquely to the tapestry of global style. For those looking for a more refined, sober and grounded take, Unvain Studios merges minimalist elegance with subtle rebellion. Their clean lines and muted color palettes offer sophisticated streetwear with a quiet edge. Meanwhile, Mki Myuki Zoku offers a minimalist aesthetic with high-end tailoring, blending simplicity with luxury. Represent strikes a similar balance, providing modern utility and a streetwear sensibility with a polished, upscale approach.
Each of these brands speaks to a different facet of urban and high fashion, from graphic streetwear to refined tailoring. But this is just a glimpse into the wider fashion landscape. 1017 ALYX 9SM, Stüssy, and Naked Wolfe further enrich this scene, while brands like 404 and Polemique reflect the growing intersection of digital culture and fashion.

Finding pieces from these brands often requires diligent “crate digging” on platforms like Grailed, Depop, Farfetch, SSENSE, Yoox, or physically by hunting through thrift stores all the way to high-end galleries. My personal favorite gallery is Vitkac in Warsaw. Which are all also extremely potent tools to discover new brands and designers. These pieces can be expensive, but if you know how to search, you can find them at affordable prices.
Here’s a curated selection of only a handful of these brands in no particular order.

Vetements: Pioneers of high-concept streetwear, Vetements is notorious for pushing boundaries. Known for their deconstructed designs, subversive takes on everyday items, and collaboration-heavy collections, finding authentic Vetements pieces can be challenging, but the brand’s radical aesthetic has made them a standout in fashion.
Gallery Dept.: Fusing art and fashion, Gallery Dept. brings an artistic, grunge-inspired approach to streetwear. The brand’s pieces are often hand-painted and distressed, offering a blend of vintage and high-fashion sensibilities. It’s a brand that’s equal parts street culture and fine art.
Lanvin: While not universally loved, Lanvin has undeniably crafted some legendary pieces, especially in the footwear department. The Curb Sneakers are a perfect example of their exploration of chunky, bold footwear. For those who appreciate refined yet contemporary designs, Lanvin offers a wealth of surprising treasures.
Diesel: stands out as a long-time mainstay in the fashion world, offering rugged yet refined designs. Known for its denim heritage, the brand consistently mixes industrial aesthetics with luxurious touches. While grounded, Diesel brings bold concepts to everyday wear, offering quality and style that endures.

Wang’s designs often blur the lines between street style and high fashion, and his ability to mix dark, gritty vibes with polished elegance makes his collections both intriguing and highly wearable.
Rough Simmons (Not to be confused with Raf Simmons): The name says it all—Rough Simmons is about raw, in-your-face fashion with a heavily avant-garde approach. Their pieces exude a sense of rebellion and boldness that challenges conventional aesthetics. It’s one for those who want fashion that makes a statement, both in its materials and design.
Raf Simmons: Raf Simons is renowned for blending youth culture with minimalist sophistication. His collections often feature clean lines, thought-provoking graphics, and an avant-garde sensibility that redefines contemporary fashion. Simons’ work resonates deeply with those who appreciate intellectual design paired with wearable art.

Whether it’s oversized silhouettes or futuristic footwear, Owens constantly plays with proportions, making his work stand out in a way few other designers can.
Kiko Kostadinov: Kiko Kostadinov stands at the forefront of the next generation of designers, mixing technical innovation with artistic vision. Known for his experimental shapes and use of unconventional fabrics, Kostadinov’s collections blur the line between fashion and architecture, offering garments that look like they were pulled from the future.
Heron Preston: A key player in the streetwear scene, Heron Preston combines high-fashion concepts with the irreverence of urban culture. His collections often incorporate bold graphics and logo-heavy pieces, pushing the boundaries of casual fashion into something more elevated.
Balenciaga: Balenciaga is a polarizing brand. While their pieces may not always be universally appealing, they certainly leave an impression. Known for transforming everyday items into high-fashion statements, Balenciaga has redefined luxury streetwear, especially with their oversized silhouettes and provocative designs. Specifically the designs by Demna.

The brand’s distinctively dark and architectural style is often paired with technical fabrics, producing a sleek and progressive aesthetic. Their balaclavas and masks, like the one I personally use, are an iconic part of their design repertoire.

Palm Angels: A highly recognizable name in luxury streetwear, Palm Angels blends skate culture with upscale design. Their collections often feature iconic graphics and bold logos, but what truly sets them apart is their ability to infuse a sense of individuality and cool factor into each piece.
Moncler: While known for their outerwear, Moncler brings a high-fashion touch to performance wear. Their collaborations with designers like Rick Owens and Giambattista Valli have solidified their place in the luxury fashion scene, but their mainstream appeal is undeniable.
Burberry: While not really my personal style, Burberry remains a staple of British luxury. Known for its iconic trench coats and checkered patterns, the brand’s newer collections often feature a mix of classic design with modern twists, keeping it relevant in today’s fashion world.
Carhartt WIP: Carhartt WIP takes the workwear brand Carhartt and transforms it for a more fashion-forward audience. The brand combines durability with streetwear sensibilities, making it an essential for those who appreciate functional, yet stylish, clothing. Carhartt on steroids (or crack) if you may.
Junya Watanabe: Known for his conceptual approach, Junya Watanabe takes traditional fashion and flips it on its head. His collections often feature experimental fabrics and unusual cuts, offering an avant-garde take on high fashion that appeals to the most daring fashion-forward individuals.
off-White: Off-White has been through ups and downs, especially after the passing of its founder Virgil Abloh, but it still holds a place in the fashion world. The brand blends luxury with streetwear, featuring graphic-heavy designs and distinctive motifs that have captured the public’s imagination.
Enfants Riches Deprimes: Ultra-stylized, Enfants Riches Deprimes brings a unique vision of luxury streetwear to life. Often adorned with luxury fabrications, the brand is all about blending opulence with rebellion, making it one of the most coveted high-end streetwear brands out there.
Acne Studios: Known for its eclectic and sometimes offbeat designs, Acne Studios brings a high-fashion edge to casual wear. Their collections often mix understated minimalism with bold graphic elements, creating a unique juxtaposition that appeals to lovers of avant-garde fashion.
Mostly Heard Rarely Seen:- A brand that blends intricate craftsmanship with streetwear sensibilities. Their use of unique textures, clever detailing, and a play on visuals gives their pieces a distinct identity. Their designs challenge norms while staying wearable, creating a perfect balance between conceptual and practical.

Once again, this is just a tiny glimpse into the immense world of brands out there. Use this as a starting point to dive deeper, explore, and discover the vast creativity and innovation that the fashion world has to offer.

OVERDXSE: This brand is the epitome of edge. Their designs don’t just push boundaries; they leap over them with an unapologetic attitude that feels authentic and raw. There’s a soulfulness to their work, a balance between grit and creativity that’s very hard to match.
READYMADE: Known for repurposing military fabrics and blending them with modern silhouettes, READYMADE is a masterclass in craftsmanship. Each piece feels deliberate, carrying an energy that speaks to its one-of-a-kind nature.
R13: This brand’s approach is as rebellious as it is refined. While their 1-of-1 offerings are more prominent in their women’s collections, their aesthetic is universally intriguing. Deconstructed denim, oversized silhouettes, and that grunge-meets-luxury vibe make them stand out.
Can’t Look/Look At Yourself: This is a young designer who channels heavy inspiration from Problemboy, but with a fresh spin. Their graphic wear feels strikingly mature for someone just starting out, blending bold visuals with a sense of experimentation. They’re definitely one to watch.
Nika Wear: Another rising star in the 1-of-1 space, Nika Wear combines unique ideas with impressive execution. There’s a sense of ambition in their work that’s impossible to overlook, and it’s exciting to see how they’re carving out a place in the scene.

Ok, now let’s address the elephant in the room: Antisocial Social Club. Sure, technically, their pieces fall into the 1-of-1 category, but let’s call it what it is—trash disguised as exclusivity. The fabric quality is abysmal, the designs are uninspired, and there’s no dedicated designer driving the brand’s vision. Their business model is even worse, relying on artificial scarcity to inflate prices and create a false sense of demand. It’s less about artistry and more about playing the resale game, which, frankly, cheapens the entire concept of 1-of-1s.
Fuck Anti Social Club, they can suck my dick.

 There exists a distinct and very specific type of anticipation—the anticipation of total coherence. The feeling that you are on the verge of stepping into a space where, for the first time, everything will finally make sense to you. Perhaps it is the lobby of a grand archive or library, where all the forgotten knowledge of humanity has been meticulously cataloged and tailored specifically so that you are able to understand it. Perhaps it is the Cargo Entrance of the Sheraton Buenos Aires. Perhaps it is the hall of an impossibly grand party, where everyone already knows who you are, and they have all been waiting for you—just you.
Or, perhaps, it is the first time you hold a Nokia 8600 Luna, in your hands.
Released in May 2007, the 8600 Luna was too beautiful to be a phone. It was a black monolith of glass and steel, a phone that lingered just outside the edge of understanding—like a sacred object in an ancient ritual, a piece of technology that seemed to hint at a future we were NEVER meant to reach.
Of course, it was all an illusion. The 8600 Luna was already obsolete upon arrival—its design a farewell, not a welcome. The moment of coherence lasted only as long as it took for your thumb to slide the keypad down—after that, the charm was lost. The world was still the world, slightly too wide, slightly too coarse, never quite as Slim as you needed it to be.




“Arguelles’ nonchalant demeanor could only be attributed to his ideological control over the spatial configurations of the slim — Or so we thought.”

Slimness, as conceived in the doctrine of Sebastian Arguelles, is not merely a question of thinness, nor a simple preference for narrow objects (albeit, it certainly includes all of these). It is a metaphysical imperative, an aesthetic and spatial philosophy that governs the very nature of things.
Indeed,
Through Arguelles, we perceive slimness as an ontological stance, an existential condition that seeps into all domains of life—architecture, fashion, technology, and even social interactions.
We now proceed to embark on an inquiry into slimness, moving from the tangible to the abstract, culminating in a rigorous mathematical formalization of its underlying principles.




“Drawing inspiration from Isamu Noguchi’s early furniture designs and Le Corbusier’s mastery of Concrete Minimalism, Arguelles set out on a journey of self-discovery. Little did he—or the world—realize that this was merely the first tremor of a revolution shaking the very foundation of existence itself.”



To understand the slimness in its proper context, we must first establish its fundamental constraints. Slimness exists only in relation to its counterpart—the non slim. A slim object is only slim insofar as it is slimmer than its reference class. We define the Arguelles’ Slimness Principle (ASP):

Definition 3.1: Arguelles’ Slimness Principle
An entity is slim if and only if, under a given reference frame, it maintains a comparative degree of thinness, narrowness, or minimalism that exceeds an arbitrary threshold defined by the observer.

This sense of relativity introduces a certain degree of paradoxicality: If all things become slim, nothing is slim. Hence, slimness is a property of contrast, and its aesthetic potency derives exactly from this juxtaposition.



While our primary goal here is to craft an abstraction that captures the essence of Slimness, it would be shortsighted—perhaps even reckless—to dive in without first laying down a solid, tangible foundation to build upon from the ground up.




Picture this:
“You stand in an impeccably arranged line, each person spaced with precision, all facing forward with quiet confidence. The entrance is a striking rectangle, far from ordinary, just wide enough to welcome the average individual. As the line inches forward, you step into what seems like a long, narrow corridor—a liminal passageway teetering between anticipation and reality. Your first instinct is that this is merely a prelude to the main event, but then the lights shift, and pulsating music erupts, jolting you from your thoughts. You lean out from the line, and there it is—a DJ booth flanked by two of the sleekest, most minimalist speakers you’ve ever encountered. And at the center of it all? The mastermind behind this experience: Arguelles. Everything is meticulously distilled to its essence—the lighting, the sound, the very atmosphere. It’s as if you’ve transcended into a realm where slimness is the ultimate law. Yet, oddly enough, you find yourself embracing this simplicity, as if everything has fallen into place in a surprising harmony. Welcome to the Slim Rave.”



Nowhere is the principle of slimness more radically manifested than in the Slim Rave, an event designed and optimized for peak Arguellesian aesthetics. Here, everything exists within extreme slender constraints, adhering to an almost pathological devotion to minimal width. Attending the Slim Rave is less about dancing or enjoying the music and more about navigating a hyper-optimized space where bodily movement itself is restructured by the tyranny of thinness.



Upon arrival, attendees are funneled through an entrance no wider than a standard doorway, single-file, much like entering a subway turnstile. Instead of the usual wristbands, guests receive an adhesive barcode strip to be attached vertically along the forearm—QR codes deemed “too thick” for the event. Security checks are conducted via a vertical scanning gate, ensuring that even the process of verification adheres to the event’s thematic obsession.



The dance corridor extends in a perfectly straight, unbroken line, measuring no wider than the narrowest Tokyo alleyway. Attendees are forced to move in single file, resulting in a unique phenomenon where front-line dancers must lead movement sequences, dictating the collective flow of the rave. This constraint, however, imposes a special form of social etiquette: a misplaced shuffle could result in a domino effect down the entire corridor.



At the heart of the rave there is an almost comically narrow DJ setup—a single Thales TTT-Slim II turntable, with space for only one hand to operate it at a time. Arguelles, clad in a form-fitting, vertically stripped ensemble, must adopt a posture akin to a tramp operator, managing sound with surgical precision relying on minimal movements. The performance by the Slim Deck™, a propietary console that compresses waveforms into elongated, ultra-slim representations, rendering bass lines as mere slivers of sound.



The propietary sound system—Skinny Flaco™ follows the principle of verticality, employing tall, slender line arrays with minimal horizontal dispersion. The bass is directional, engineered to travel in compressed beams, creating an unusual pocketed sound environment where low frequences feel almost intangible unless one aligns perfectly within the designated acoustic “sweet spot”.



Lighting is reduced to its purest linear essence—sharp, vertical beams slicing through the space like laser projections. LED strips trace the periphery, pulsating in synchronized gradients of white and electr-ic blue. There are no strobes, no excessive fixtures, only controlled illumination that enhances the perceived depth of the already slim venue.



All beverages are served in test tubes—cocktails distilled into vertically elongated ampoules, requiring drinkers to tilt their heads at extreme angles to consume. Food options are similarly constrained, consisting exclusively of stick-shaped rations.
The following is a tentative list of food and drink offerings specifically catered for this event.

The VIP guests may access the HyperSlim Lounge, an elevated platform, reinforced by galvanized steel, spanning no wider than a plank bridge. Here, visitors recline on elongated chaise lounges while sipping from thin flutes of liquid nitrogen-cooled vodka. Conversation is discouraged unless conducted in hushed, elongated syllables.

“We tried to take the Colimit of the Slim but it Collapsed into a One-Dimensional Line — This challenges the very foundations of our understanding!”



Slimness, despite its aesthetic and spatial implications, is fundamentally about [structure]: the preservation of an essential form while eliminating excess. However, its interpretation is inherently context-dependent—what is considered slim in one domain (architecture, fashion, or even raves) may not translate directly to another. Thus, a rigorous mathematical framework is necessary, one that captures the relational nature of slimness rather than treating it as a fixed property.
Category theory provides a natural language for this endeavor. Instead of defining slimness in absolute terms, we construct a category of slim objects, where an object’s slimness is determined by its morphisms—how it relates to other objects, rather than its intrinsic measurements. This shift allows us to generalize the concept across different domains and study transformations of slimness rather than static definitions.
Before we begin to encode these ideas, let’s introduce the necessary definitions.

Definition 4.1: Yoneda’s Lemma (Condensed Definition)
Let \(\mathcal{C}\) be a category, and \(X\) be an object in \(\mathcal{C}\). For any functor \(\mathcal{F}: \mathcal{C}^{\text{op}} \to \text{Set}\), the Yoneda Lemma asserts the following natural isomorphism:
\[
\text{Nat}(\text{Hom}(-, X), \mathcal{F}) \cong \mathcal{F}(X)
\]
This means that the set of natural transformations between the representable functor \(\text{Hom}(-, X)\) and any other functor \(\mathcal{F}\) is naturally isomorphic to the set of elements of \(\mathcal{F}\) evaluated at \(X\).

Furthermore, we will also utilize the following definition.

Definition 4.2: Yoneda Embedding (Condensed Definition)
Let \(\mathcal{C}\) be a locally small category and \(\mathbf{Set}\) the category of sets. The \(\textbf{Yoneda embedding}\) is a functor:
\[
\mathbf{Y}: \mathcal{C} \to \mathbf{Set}^{\mathcal{C}^{\text{op}}}
\]
defined as follows: for each object \(A \in \mathcal{C}\), the functor \(\mathbf{Y}(A)\) is the representable functor \(\mathrm{Hom}(-,A): \mathcal{C}^{\text{op}} \to \mathbf{Set}\), i.e.,
\[
\mathbf{Y}(A) = \mathrm{Hom}(-,A)
\]
For each morphism \(f: A \to B\) in \(\mathcal{C}\), the map \(\mathbf{Y}(f)\) is induced by the natural transformation:
\[
\mathbf{Y}(f): \mathrm{Hom}(-,A) \to \mathrm{Hom}(-,B)
\]
where \(\mathbf{Y}(f)(g) = f \circ g\) for \(g \in \mathrm{Hom}(C,A)\), ensuring the functor is covariant.

We are now sufficiently equipped to work on this foundation.




“How deeply disheartening, my child. My trust was yours, and yet, the promise of lacerating your form into the singularity of a one-dimensional existence remains unfulfilled. In this betrayal, you have not only lost a son but cast an interminable shadow of regret. Disappointment weighs heavily upon us both.” —Arguelles to his mother. Circa 2022

Though unconventional in its structure, this section will be organized into multiple subsections to ensure clarity and readability. We formalize a category \(\mathcal{S}\), where:


Objects \(X \in \mathcal{S}\) are all conceivable entities, physical and conceptual (e.g., raves, architecture, cigarettes, mathematics).


Morphisms between objects are constrained by a Slimness Functor \(S: \mathcal{S} \to \mathbf{Set}\), which extracts the degree of slimness each object possesses.



\[S(X) = \text{Slimness Profile of } X\]

Example morphisms:


A regular nightclub \(N\) maps to a slim club \(S(N)\), preserving only its narrowest corridors, tightest leather pants, and elongated bar counters.


A non-slim object \(X\) (e.g., a bulky gaming PC) maps to its slimmest possible projection \(S(X)\), yielding something like an M1 MacBook Air or a folded napkin.


The Slim Rave \(R\) is an initial object in this category—it represents maximal slimness.












Yoneda’s Lemma tells us that we never perceive objects directly, only through their relationships (i.e., morphisms). In this case:
Slimness is defined entirely by how it transforms other things.
Since every object’s existence is dictated by its slimness projections, Arguelles’ perception acts as a Yoneda embedding:
\[\mathcal{S}(X) \cong \text{Hom}(-, S(X))\]
This implies that:

The essence of slimness is encoded in the morphisms from any object into the Slim Rave.
Arguelles does not see non-slim things at all—they have no morphisms in this system.
Reality, as perceived by Arguelles, is slimness itself.












A category often has a terminal object \(T\), such that for every object \(X\), there exists a unique morphism:
\[X \to T\]
If we assume that slimness is a maximization process, then there exists a final form of slimness that absorbs all things. We call this object \(\Omega\), the Ultimate Slim.
This means that every object in the category eventually maps into \(\Omega\), leading to a total collapse where:
\[\forall X \in \mathcal{S}, \quad X \to \Omega\]
Thus:

The Slim Rave is only a step toward \(\Omega\), the pure singularity of slimness.
In the idealized limit, \(\Omega\) is so slim that it no longer exists in any observable dimension—it is the null object.
Arguelles, as a perceptual functor, becomes blind to existence itself, as everything he sees has been mapped into nothingness.

At this point, the concept of slimness self-annihilates:
\[\textbf{If slimness is everything, then slimness is nothing.}\]











This total collapse implies that for slimness to remain meaningful, it must have a counterforce.
We introduce a dual category \(\mathcal{A}\), representing anti-slimness, where:

Objects are bulky, excessive, baroque, overflowing.
Morphisms are thickenings rather than reductions.
The initial object is Maximal Bulk, \(B\), the opposite of \(\Omega\).

The interplay between \(\mathcal{S}\) and \(\mathcal{A}\) creates a dialectical struggle:

The Slim Functor attempts to collapse everything into \(\Omega\).
The Anti-Slim Functor attempts to resist and expand objects away from \(\Omega\).
The result is a tension—a dynamic equilibrium where slimness remains distinct.

Thus we conclude:
\[\textbf{Slimness cannot exist in pure isolation—it requires resistance to remain meaningful.}\]

“There is an order to the names below, but it is not alphabetical. Nor is it chronological. Nor is it rational in any conventional sense. The pattern exists, but only for those who can perceive it.”

This work was not the product of a single mind but rather the culmination of a collective, a council of thinkers, explorers, and conceptual terrorists that have been operating for years. Their contributions, both direct and indirect, shaped the very foundations of this text. This wouldn’t be possible without you.

John Nash (But Slimmed Down) – A demon, A scholar, A reckless intellectual renegade. A visionary architect of abstraction and one of the original masterminds behind the Slim. His ability to navigate the most convoluted mental corridors has inspired the formalization of concepts that should, by all means, remain unformalized. Together, we have structured thoughts that were never meant to be structured, and yet here they stand, defying coherence. Without him, this would be a much less intellectually deranged, and therefore much less complete, work.
Bad Sound (Architect of the Illegal Frequencies) – An acoustic Warlord, an auditory pioneer, an explorer of the psychoacoustic unknown, and one of the foundational minds behind the Slim. A curator of the fundamentally incomprehensible, he has shaped sound, weaponized distortion, and turned the act of listening into an exercise in survival. Operating on a frequency regular people can’t even hear, his contributions transcend mere dialogue; they are experiments in perception itself. Many of the ideas in this work were forged through sound, through music, through the absurd resonance of sound waves that normal minds would dare not interpret. The Slim owes much of its sonic and conceptual DNA to his relentless pursuit of the strange.
Militar Mayorista Triple Esquina (High Priest of Tactical Insanity) – A structural stabilizer. A cognitive arsonist. A military-grade memetic hazard. A necessary tether to the world that still adheres to conventional logic, and yet still, a key architect of the Slim itself. As one of its original creators, he exists as both a participant in the madness and an observer of its consequences. A bridge between chaos and coherence, between the deranged dreamscapes we inhabit and the pragmatism required to interface with the uninitiated. He ensures that at least some of this makes sense—at least marginally.
(.)-za (The Ghost in the System) – An ancient force. A spectral entity. A revenant of past insanity. A pioneer, a true progenitor of the Slim. Though years have passed since his last direct contribution, his provocative thoughts and radical ideals continue to ripple through this work. He was always an anomaly—a curiosity who reminded us that embracing the unexpected leads to revelations, sometimes profound, sometimes absurd, but always worth exploring. His influence remains, ghostly yet undeniable, woven into the very fabric of the text.
RGN (The Unwitting Prophet) – A signal from the future, a transmission of curiosity that arrived when I least expected it. Though her only direct contribution was naming Arguelles’ sound system Skinny Flaco, the sheer fact that she took interest in this deranged conceptual web was enough to shake my own foundations. Perhaps this is not merely the fever dream of a select few. Perhaps the Slim is something that can be understood, shared, and expanded beyond its initial enclave. Even at her young age, RGN exhibits an alarming capacity for diving headfirst into the intellectual abyss. This gives me hope for her and many others. May her curiosity for the unknown guide her deeper into this labyrinth, where further madness—and inventive awakening—awaits.
C.U. – A master of the culinary craft, a Top Tier Chef and Baker whose expertise was instrumental in the development of the Slim Menu. This individual looked at the conceptual framework of the Slim and said: “What if we could ingest it? – The diner’s taste buds need to experience liminal culinary distress” Inspired by the avant-garde experimentation of the Danish restaurant Alchemist, his insights helped distill the gastronomic essence of slimness into something one could theoretically consume—if they dared.
S.D. – A mathematician of the highest caliber, a former professor of mine whose keen eye ensured the mathematical integrity of this text. Without his scrutiny, the Slimness Principle may have collapsed under the weight of its own absurdity. Instead, it stands. Perhaps too tall. Perhaps too narrow. But it stands.

To all of them, my deepest and most sincere gratitude. This was never a solitary endeavor—it was a conspiracy of minds. An absurd inside joke that somehow spiraled into an academic pursuit. And should Arguelles himself one day read this, know that we remain vigilant—both in mind and body, watching, waiting. The Slim will persist.

There exists a distinct and very specific type of anticipation—the anticipation of total coherence. The feeling that you are on the verge of stepping into a space where, for the first time, everything will finally make sense to you. Perhaps it is the lobby of a grand archive or library, where all the forgotten knowledge of humanity has been meticulously cataloged and tailored specifically so that you are able to understand it. Perhaps it is the Cargo Entrance of the Sheraton Buenos Aires. Perhaps it is the hall of an impossibly grand party, where everyone already knows who you are, and they have all been waiting for you—just you.
Or, perhaps, it is the first time you hold a Nokia 8600 Luna, in your hands.
Released in May 2007, the 8600 Luna was too beautiful to be a phone. It was a black monolith of glass and steel, a phone that lingered just outside the edge of understanding—like a sacred object in an ancient ritual, a piece of technology that seemed to hint at a future we were NEVER meant to reach.
Of course, it was all an illusion. The 8600 Luna was already obsolete upon arrival—its design a farewell, not a welcome. The moment of coherence lasted only as long as it took for your thumb to slide the keypad down—after that, the charm was lost. The world was still the world, slightly too wide, slightly too coarse, never quite as Slim as you needed it to be.

“Arguelles’ nonchalant demeanor could only be attributed to his ideological control over the spatial configurations of the slim — Or so we thought.”

Slimness, as conceived in the doctrine of Sebastian Arguelles, is not merely a question of thinness, nor a simple preference for narrow objects (albeit, it certainly includes all of these). It is a metaphysical imperative, an aesthetic and spatial philosophy that governs the very nature of things.
Indeed,
Through Arguelles, we perceive slimness as an ontological stance, an existential condition that seeps into all domains of life—architecture, fashion, technology, and even social interactions.
We now proceed to embark on an inquiry into slimness, moving from the tangible to the abstract, culminating in a rigorous mathematical formalization of its underlying principles.

“Drawing inspiration from Isamu Noguchi’s early furniture designs and Le Corbusier’s mastery of Concrete Minimalism, Arguelles set out on a journey of self-discovery. Little did he—or the world—realize that this was merely the first tremor of a revolution shaking the very foundation of existence itself.”



To understand the slimness in its proper context, we must first establish its fundamental constraints. Slimness exists only in relation to its counterpart—the non slim. A slim object is only slim insofar as it is slimmer than its reference class. We define the Arguelles’ Slimness Principle (ASP):

Definition 3.1: Arguelles’ Slimness Principle
An entity is slim if and only if, under a given reference frame, it maintains a comparative degree of thinness, narrowness, or minimalism that exceeds an arbitrary threshold defined by the observer.

This sense of relativity introduces a certain degree of paradoxicality: If all things become slim, nothing is slim. Hence, slimness is a property of contrast, and its aesthetic potency derives exactly from this juxtaposition.



While our primary goal here is to craft an abstraction that captures the essence of Slimness, it would be shortsighted—perhaps even reckless—to dive in without first laying down a solid, tangible foundation to build upon from the ground up.




Picture this:
“You stand in an impeccably arranged line, each person spaced with precision, all facing forward with quiet confidence. The entrance is a striking rectangle, far from ordinary, just wide enough to welcome the average individual. As the line inches forward, you step into what seems like a long, narrow corridor—a liminal passageway teetering between anticipation and reality. Your first instinct is that this is merely a prelude to the main event, but then the lights shift, and pulsating music erupts, jolting you from your thoughts. You lean out from the line, and there it is—a DJ booth flanked by two of the sleekest, most minimalist speakers you’ve ever encountered. And at the center of it all? The mastermind behind this experience: Arguelles. Everything is meticulously distilled to its essence—the lighting, the sound, the very atmosphere. It’s as if you’ve transcended into a realm where slimness is the ultimate law. Yet, oddly enough, you find yourself embracing this simplicity, as if everything has fallen into place in a surprising harmony. Welcome to the Slim Rave.”



Nowhere is the principle of slimness more radically manifested than in the Slim Rave, an event designed and optimized for peak Arguellesian aesthetics. Here, everything exists within extreme slender constraints, adhering to an almost pathological devotion to minimal width. Attending the Slim Rave is less about dancing or enjoying the music and more about navigating a hyper-optimized space where bodily movement itself is restructured by the tyranny of thinness.



Upon arrival, attendees are funneled through an entrance no wider than a standard doorway, single-file, much like entering a subway turnstile. Instead of the usual wristbands, guests receive an adhesive barcode strip to be attached vertically along the forearm—QR codes deemed “too thick” for the event. Security checks are conducted via a vertical scanning gate, ensuring that even the process of verification adheres to the event’s thematic obsession.



The dance corridor extends in a perfectly straight, unbroken line, measuring no wider than the narrowest Tokyo alleyway. Attendees are forced to move in single file, resulting in a unique phenomenon where front-line dancers must lead movement sequences, dictating the collective flow of the rave. This constraint, however, imposes a special form of social etiquette: a misplaced shuffle could result in a domino effect down the entire corridor.



At the heart of the rave there is an almost comically narrow DJ setup—a single Thales TTT-Slim II turntable, with space for only one hand to operate it at a time. Arguelles, clad in a form-fitting, vertically stripped ensemble, must adopt a posture akin to a tramp operator, managing sound with surgical precision relying on minimal movements. The performance by the Slim Deck™, a propietary console that compresses waveforms into elongated, ultra-slim representations, rendering bass lines as mere slivers of sound.



The propietary sound system—Skinny Flaco™ follows the principle of verticality, employing tall, slender line arrays with minimal horizontal dispersion. The bass is directional, engineered to travel in compressed beams, creating an unusual pocketed sound environment where low frequences feel almost intangible unless one aligns perfectly within the designated acoustic “sweet spot”.



Lighting is reduced to its purest linear essence—sharp, vertical beams slicing through the space like laser projections. LED strips trace the periphery, pulsating in synchronized gradients of white and electr-ic blue. There are no strobes, no excessive fixtures, only controlled illumination that enhances the perceived depth of the already slim venue.



All beverages are served in test tubes—cocktails distilled into vertically elongated ampoules, requiring drinkers to tilt their heads at extreme angles to consume. Food options are similarly constrained, consisting exclusively of stick-shaped rations.
The following is a tentative list of food and drink offerings specifically catered for this event.

Slim Nigiri (Shinagiru-zushi, 品切る寿司) — Rice grains arranged in a single-file line, with fish sliced to an almost translucent state.

Dehydrated Slim Olives – Pitted olives that have been flattened into thin, crisp discs.
Micro Crackers – Wasa-style crispbreads cut into needle-thin shards.

Ultra-Thin Mille-Feuille – A mille-feuille pastry reduced to an extreme degree, with each layer measuring fractions of a millimeter.
2D Gelato Slices – Gelato frozen into ultra-thin sheets and served in perforated wafers.
Single-Thread Cotton Candy – A solitary spun sugar filament, served on a 3-meter-long skewer.


Test Tube Cocktails – Liquids served exclusively in test tubes, eliminating excess volume.
Capillary-Action Espresso – A shot of espresso delivered through a narrow capillary system, allowing for an ultra-thin extraction process.
Linear Shochu (線状焼酎, Senjō Shōchū) – A distilled spirit that is sipped through an elongated, hair-thin pipette, forcing controlled intake.
Thin Ice Martinis – Martinis served with ice sheets measuring under 2 mm in thickness, designed to dissolve almost immediately.






The VIP guests may access the HyperSlim Lounge, an elevated platform, reinforced by galvanized steel, spanning no wider than a plank bridge. Here, visitors recline on elongated chaise lounges while sipping from thin flutes of liquid nitrogen-cooled vodka. Conversation is discouraged unless conducted in hushed, elongated syllables.

Despite its rigid adherence to spatial constraints, the Slim Rave is not merely a thought experiment but a plausible venue—an actual physical space that could be constructed (albeit with some challenging ergonomical installations). As we transition from tangible descriptions into abstraction, we confront the question: How far can we decompose slimness before it ceases to be? If we reduce the Slim Rave to its most elementary components, we are left with a single line, a one-dimensional experience of music, movement, and presence.
Here arises the Atomic Rave Theory (ART): The claim that all raves can be reduced to an atomic irreducible slim state. If taken to its logical extreme, does the Slim Rave still function as a rave? What does Arguelles see that we do not? At the subatomic level, does slimness persist?


This is where “TheSlim” transcends its comedic origins and enters the realm of epistemology and perception. Slimness, as we conceive it, is an abstraction—it is not merely a measure of width but a function of expectation. If we accept that slimness is relative, then its perceived intensity depends on the observer’s baseline.
To us, the Slim Rave is absurdly narrow—a brutal distillation of space and experience. But what if it is not slim enough for Arguelles? What if his threshold for slimness exists at a level of abstraction beyond our comprehension?
Perhaps, to him, our version of the Slim Rave is still bloated, indulgent, grotesquely excessive in its spatial permissiveness. Maybe true slimness is asymptotic—an ideal that can never be fully realized, only approached in increasingly austere refinements.

What does it mean for the rave to be this slim? What is Arguelles’ vision, and why does he insist on reducing the world around him to this essential, minimal form?

Does he view everything in his life in the same way, reducing people, places, and objects to their purest form?



Could it be that Arguelles sees slimness not as a choice, but as an inevitability—the very framework of existence itself?



If we imagine the rave on an atomic level, it becomes even more bizarre: how does the concept of slimness apply when we zoom in so far? Could we see the rave as a singular, atomized entity, where everything—the sound, the people, the room itself—is compressed into the most efficient version of itself, leaving no space for ambiguity or superfluous detail? Does Arguelles see the world in a similarly atomized way? Is every decision, every action, an attempt to distill existence to its most pure, most efficient form?

The rave, the people, the music—they all become reflections of a larger, almost mathematical concept of minimalism and reductionism. If Arguelles perceives reality at an atomic level, then his standard for slimness might not even exist on a human scale. He does not see a slim cigarette—he sees the space between molecules, the inefficiency of matter itself. What we consider slim, he considers wide. If this is true, then his ideal rave is no rave at all—perhaps just a single sine wave, an auditory singularity, the theoretical limit of musical slimness.
Thus, we must ask: are we capable of truly understanding Arguelles’ vision, or are we condemned to misinterpret it, forever constructing raves that are too wide? If so, then the Slim Rave, rather than being a celebration of slimness, is a tragic testament to our failure. We can only approximate slimness, never attain it.

“We tried to take the Colimit of the Slim but it Collapsed into a One-Dimensional Line — This challenges the very foundations of our understanding!”



Slimness, despite its aesthetic and spatial implications, is fundamentally about [structure]: the preservation of an essential form while eliminating excess. However, its interpretation is inherently context-dependent—what is considered slim in one domain (architecture, fashion, or even raves) may not translate directly to another. Thus, a rigorous mathematical framework is necessary, one that captures the relational nature of slimness rather than treating it as a fixed property.
Category theory provides a natural language for this endeavor. Instead of defining slimness in absolute terms, we construct a category of slim objects, where an object’s slimness is determined by its morphisms—how it relates to other objects, rather than its intrinsic measurements. This shift allows us to generalize the concept across different domains and study transformations of slimness rather than static definitions.
Before we begin to encode these ideas, let’s introduce the necessary definitions.

Definition 4.1: Yoneda’s Lemma (Condensed Definition)
Let \(\mathcal{C}\) be a category, and \(X\) be an object in \(\mathcal{C}\). For any functor \(\mathcal{F}: \mathcal{C}^{\text{op}} \to \text{Set}\), the Yoneda Lemma asserts the following natural isomorphism:
\[
\text{Nat}(\text{Hom}(-, X), \mathcal{F}) \cong \mathcal{F}(X)
\]
This means that the set of natural transformations between the representable functor \(\text{Hom}(-, X)\) and any other functor \(\mathcal{F}\) is naturally isomorphic to the set of elements of \(\mathcal{F}\) evaluated at \(X\).

Furthermore, we will also utilize the following definition.

Definition 4.2: Yoneda Embedding (Condensed Definition)
Let \(\mathcal{C}\) be a locally small category and \(\mathbf{Set}\) the category of sets. The \(\textbf{Yoneda embedding}\) is a functor:
\[
\mathbf{Y}: \mathcal{C} \to \mathbf{Set}^{\mathcal{C}^{\text{op}}}
\]
defined as follows: for each object \(A \in \mathcal{C}\), the functor \(\mathbf{Y}(A)\) is the representable functor \(\mathrm{Hom}(-,A): \mathcal{C}^{\text{op}} \to \mathbf{Set}\), i.e.,
\[
\mathbf{Y}(A) = \mathrm{Hom}(-,A)
\]
For each morphism \(f: A \to B\) in \(\mathcal{C}\), the map \(\mathbf{Y}(f)\) is induced by the natural transformation:
\[
\mathbf{Y}(f): \mathrm{Hom}(-,A) \to \mathrm{Hom}(-,B)
\]
where \(\mathbf{Y}(f)(g) = f \circ g\) for \(g \in \mathrm{Hom}(C,A)\), ensuring the functor is covariant.

We are now sufficiently equipped to work on this foundation.




“How deeply disheartening, my child. My trust was yours, and yet, the promise of lacerating your form into the singularity of a one-dimensional existence remains unfulfilled. In this betrayal, you have not only lost a son but cast an interminable shadow of regret. Disappointment weighs heavily upon us both.” —Arguelles to his mother. Circa 2022

Though unconventional in its structure, this section will be organized into multiple subsections to ensure clarity and readability. Each subsection will address a distinct component of the formalization, progressively building on the overarching framework. It’s important to take into consideration that every subsection follows directly from the previous one. (Yes this whole text is a hyperlink)






We formalize a category \(\mathcal{S}\), where:


Objects \(X \in \mathcal{S}\) are all conceivable entities, physical and conceptual (e.g., raves, architecture, cigarettes, mathematics).


Morphisms between objects are constrained by a Slimness Functor \(S: \mathcal{S} \to \mathbf{Set}\), which extracts the degree of slimness each object possesses.



\[S(X) = \text{Slimness Profile of } X\]

Example morphisms:


A regular nightclub \(N\) maps to a slim club \(S(N)\), preserving only its narrowest corridors, tightest leather pants, and elongated bar counters.


A non-slim object \(X\) (e.g., a bulky gaming PC) maps to its slimmest possible projection \(S(X)\), yielding something like an M1 MacBook Air or a folded napkin.


The Slim Rave \(R\) is an initial object in this category—it represents maximal slimness.












Yoneda’s Lemma tells us that we never perceive objects directly, only through their relationships (i.e., morphisms). In this case:
Slimness is defined entirely by how it transforms other things.
Since every object’s existence is dictated by its slimness projections, Arguelles’ perception acts as a Yoneda embedding:
\[\mathcal{S}(X) \cong \text{Hom}(-, S(X))\]
This implies that:

The essence of slimness is encoded in the morphisms from any object into the Slim Rave.
Arguelles does not see non-slim things at all—they have no morphisms in this system.
Reality, as perceived by Arguelles, is slimness itself.












A category often has a terminal object \(T\), such that for every object \(X\), there exists a unique morphism:
\[X \to T\]
If we assume that slimness is a maximization process, then there exists a final form of slimness that absorbs all things. We call this object \(\Omega\), the Ultimate Slim.
This means that every object in the category eventually maps into \(\Omega\), leading to a total collapse where:
\[\forall X \in \mathcal{S}, \quad X \to \Omega\]
Thus:

The Slim Rave is only a step toward \(\Omega\), the pure singularity of slimness.
In the idealized limit, \(\Omega\) is so slim that it no longer exists in any observable dimension—it is the null object.
Arguelles, as a perceptual functor, becomes blind to existence itself, as everything he sees has been mapped into nothingness.

At this point, the concept of slimness self-annihilates:
\[\textbf{If slimness is everything, then slimness is nothing.}\]











This total collapse implies that for slimness to remain meaningful, it must have a counterforce.
We introduce a dual category \(\mathcal{A}\), representing anti-slimness, where:

Objects are bulky, excessive, baroque, overflowing.
Morphisms are thickenings rather than reductions.
The initial object is Maximal Bulk, \(B\), the opposite of \(\Omega\).

The interplay between \(\mathcal{S}\) and \(\mathcal{A}\) creates a dialectical struggle:

The Slim Functor attempts to collapse everything into \(\Omega\).
The Anti-Slim Functor attempts to resist and expand objects away from \(\Omega\).
The result is a tension—a dynamic equilibrium where slimness remains distinct.

Thus we conclude:
\[\textbf{Slimness cannot exist in pure isolation—it requires resistance to remain meaningful.}\]







R.P.: WAIT, WAIT, WAIT—hold the fuck up. So all this Math bullshit. ALL OF IT. It makes sense? What the fuck. Like, is this real?


L.F.P.: Well, haha, that is a really good question. I guess it depends what exactly you mean by “real”. See, in pure mathematics, we aren’t bounded by physical intuition—we care about constructing rigorous, self-consistent farmeworks. The structures we define exist within their own formal systems, governed by axioms and logical inference. As long as our definitions hold up and we don’t run into contradictions, the mathematics is valid. It is “real”, even if that reality only exists within a carefully defined framework.


R.P.: Okay… okay. That is insane to me. Keep going.








If Arguelles is truly an ultimate observer of slimness, then he cannot perceive Anti-Slimness at all.
Thus, the question remains:

Does Arguelles’ perception cause the collapse into \(\Omega\)?
Or is he merely an agent accelerating the collapse?
If he becomes aware of Anti-Slimness, does he reject it—or does he recognize the necessity of the dialectic?
Does observation define reality? Or does reality limit what can be observed?


 Well I don’t fucking know. 

We leave these questions as open problems that we may, or may not, explore in future entries.

“There is an order to the names below, but it is not alphabetical. Nor is it chronological. Nor is it rational in any conventional sense. The pattern exists, but only for those who can perceive it.”

This work was not the product of a single mind but rather the culmination of a collective, a council of thinkers, explorers, and conceptual terrorists that have been operating for years. Their contributions, both direct and indirect, shaped the very foundations of this text. This wouldn’t be possible without you.

John Nash (But Slimmed Down) – A demon, A scholar, A reckless intellectual renegade. A visionary architect of abstraction and one of the original masterminds behind the Slim. His ability to navigate the most convoluted mental corridors has inspired the formalization of concepts that should, by all means, remain unformalized. Together, we have structured thoughts that were never meant to be structured, and yet here they stand, defying coherence. Without him, this would be a much less intellectually deranged, and therefore much less complete, work.
Bad Sound (Architect of the Illegal Frequencies) – An acoustic Warlord, an auditory pioneer, an explorer of the psychoacoustic unknown, and one of the foundational minds behind the Slim. A curator of the fundamentally incomprehensible, he has shaped sound, weaponized distortion, and turned the act of listening into an exercise in survival. Operating on a frequency regular people can’t even hear, his contributions transcend mere dialogue; they are experiments in perception itself. Many of the ideas in this work were forged through sound, through music, through the absurd resonance of sound waves that normal minds would dare not interpret. The Slim owes much of its sonic and conceptual DNA to his relentless pursuit of the strange.
Militar Mayorista Triple Esquina (High Priest of Tactical Insanity) – A structural stabilizer. A cognitive arsonist. A military-grade memetic hazard. A necessary tether to the world that still adheres to conventional logic, and yet still, a key architect of the Slim itself. As one of its original creators, he exists as both a participant in the madness and an observer of its consequences. A bridge between chaos and coherence, between the deranged dreamscapes we inhabit and the pragmatism required to interface with the uninitiated. He ensures that at least some of this makes sense—at least marginally.
(.)-za (The Ghost in the System) – An ancient force. A spectral entity. A revenant of past insanity. A pioneer, a true progenitor of the Slim. Though years have passed since his last direct contribution, his provocative thoughts and radical ideals continue to ripple through this work. He was always an anomaly—a curiosity who reminded us that embracing the unexpected leads to revelations, sometimes profound, sometimes absurd, but always worth exploring. His influence remains, ghostly yet undeniable, woven into the very fabric of the text.
RGN (The Unwitting Prophet) – A signal from the future, a transmission of curiosity that arrived when I least expected it. Though her only direct contribution was naming Arguelles’ sound system Skinny Flaco, the sheer fact that she took interest in this deranged conceptual web was enough to shake my own foundations. Perhaps this is not merely the fever dream of a select few. Perhaps the Slim is something that can be understood, shared, and expanded beyond its initial enclave. Even at her young age, RGN exhibits an alarming capacity for diving headfirst into the intellectual abyss. This gives me hope for her and many others. May her curiosity for the unknown guide her deeper into this labyrinth, where further madness—and inventive awakening—awaits.
C.U. – A master of the culinary craft, a Top Tier Chef and Baker whose expertise was instrumental in the development of the Slim Menu. This individual looked at the conceptual framework of the Slim and said: “What if we could ingest it? – The diner’s taste buds need to experience liminal culinary distress” Inspired by the avant-garde experimentation of the Danish restaurant Alchemist, his insights helped distill the gastronomic essence of slimness into something one could theoretically consume—if they dared.
S.D. – A mathematician of the highest caliber, a former professor of mine whose keen eye ensured the mathematical integrity of this text. Without his scrutiny, the Slimness Principle may have collapsed under the weight of its own absurdity. Instead, it stands. Perhaps too tall. Perhaps too narrow. But it stands.

To all of them, my deepest and most sincere gratitude. This was never a solitary endeavor—it was a conspiracy of minds. An absurd inside joke that somehow spiraled into an academic pursuit. And should Arguelles himself one day read this, know that we remain vigilant—both in mind and body, watching, waiting. The Slim will persist.



 2025 AcidBaby.
